paper.title: Algorithm 681: INTBIS, a portable interval Newton/bisection package for finding all solutions of nonlinear systems (collected algorithm, title from the frame item)
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/681.gz (ACM article not read; ACM pages return 403 from this host)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 681.gz (fetched by scout 2026-11-27 into a fresh /tmp directory; decompressed and read as text, not executed).
code.note: Single text file of about 11,560 lines: documentation, the Fortran sources (GENBIS driver, INPUT, OUTPUT, ROOTS, FTESTH, HNSNG, POLFUN and related routines, INTARI, STKMAN, LPKD1M), the sample input (NPROBLEMS = 9, test problem no. 1 cubic-parabola at about line 9718) and the sample output run for all nine problems (from about line 10380; the block for problem 1 reads 'Test problem no. 1: cubic-parabola' then 'Number of roots found: 3', 'Number of leaves: 6'). The documentation calls the sample output file TOMS86SH.OU1; this text is the concatenation that ships, not a separate file.

field: numerics (interval Newton and bisection for nonlinear systems)

claim.location: Shipped sample output of the GENBIS driver in the archive: the block for 'Test problem no. 1: cubic-parabola' (about line 10398 of the decompressed text), field 'Number of roots found'. The input is the NPROBLEMS=9 sample data set at about line 9718, first problem.

reference.file: sample output block inside 681.gz (decompressed text, not a separate member)
reference.sha256: not computed for the block; the value is quoted here and compared as an integer

claim.metric: Number of roots found by ROOTS for test problem no. 1 (cubic-parabola), as printed by GENBIS.
claim.paper_value: The paper's own test table is not read (ACM 403). The shipped sample output is the reference.

values.name: test problem 1 cubic-parabola, number of roots found

tolerance.basis: The quantity is an integer count of boxes resolved as unique roots by a deterministic bisection with fixed tolerances (EPSMIN 1e-5, EPSF 1e-10, MAXFT 10000 in the shipped configuration). Any change in the count is a real change in the computed result, so no slack is allowed. Fixed now, before any run; not to be loosened after a run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute for problem 1 (the shipped run of all nine problems takes about 4 seconds, per the documentation).
cost.data_size: None; the sample input is inside the archive.
cost.data_licence: No data. Source is the public netlib TOMS collected-algorithms archive.

why: The package runs a deterministic interval Newton and bisection search on a small nonlinear system with an integer root count the code must compute; the rerun needs the Fortran build and the embedded configuration.
